get.description: List available datasets from sql-warehouse.

Diff a context's stored schema snapshot against the live warehouse tables.

Read-only — never fails on drift itself; an unreachable table surfaces as a
``TABLE_NOT_FOUND`` finding with HTTP 200, not an error response. Column
checks (``DESCRIBE``) always run; type checks (``SELECT DISTINCT``, a full
table scan) only run when ``check_types=true``.

The ``proposed`` snapshot in the response can be echoed back verbatim through
``PUT /graph-contexts/{id}`` to apply the resync — this endpoint never writes.

Warehouse-only: drift is the gap between a context's stored table snapshot
and the live tables. A schemaless graph database has neither, so those
contexts reject this outright rather than reporting a vacuous "no drift".

post.description: Get a subgraph for a graph context.

Fetch properties for a known set of node ids.

Backs progressive loading: the client renders a graph returned with
``nodes_mode='types'`` immediately, then fills in properties in background
batches through this endpoint.

The projection comes from the context's configured ``node_properties``. An
optional ``columns`` list may NARROW it further (unknown names are dropped),
which matters on wide tables: fetching all 100 columns for every node costs
more than the single request progressive loading replaced.

BFS expansion from a node.

Expands from a starting node following edges up to the specified depth.
Supports both directed (follows edge direction) and undirected (both directions).

Args:
    data.node_id: Starting node ID
    data.depth: Expansion depth (1-2)
    data.edge_limit: Max edges to return (4-1000)
    data.directed: If True, only follow edge direction (src->dst)
    data.edge_types: Filter by edge types (empty = all types)

Execute a graph query (SQL) and return matching nodes/edges.

The query should use tables in catalog.schema.table format.
Use the context's edge_table_name and node_table_name for queries.

Example queries:
- SELECT * FROM dev_catalog.graphs.edges_test WHERE relationship_type = 'KNOWS'
- SELECT * FROM dev_catalog.graphs.edges_test e JOIN dev_catalog.graphs.nodes_test n ON e.src = n.node_id

SQL-backed contexts only — a native graph database has no SQL surface.

Execute an OpenCypher query and return matching nodes/edges.

On a SQL warehouse the query is transpiled to Spark SQL by gsql2rsql; on a
native graph database it runs as-is and ``transpiled_sql`` comes back null.

Example queries:
- MATCH (n:Person) RETURN n
- MATCH (a:Person)-[r:KNOWS]->(b:Person) RETURN a, r, b

Run a generic query and return raw tabular rows (columns + rows).

Unlike ``/cypher``, the query is NOT required to return edges — any
projection is allowed (e.g. ``MATCH (n:Person) RETURN n.name, count(*)``).
In ``cypher`` mode a SQL backend transpiles the query first; ``sql`` mode
runs it directly and is rejected outright by non-SQL backends. Both modes
are restricted to read-only statements.

get.description:
Poll an in-flight table query submitted via ``POST .../query/table``.

Returns ``status="running"`` while the backend is still executing, or
``status="succeeded"`` with the raw rows once complete. A CANCELED statement
returns ``status="canceled"``; a FAILED one raises HTTP 400.

post.description:
Cancel an in-flight table query, releasing the backend's compute.

Best-effort and idempotent: cancelling an already-finished statement is a
no-op.
Submit a SQL graph query as a cancellable, progress-reporting job.
Submit an OpenCypher graph query as a cancellable, progress job.

get.description:
Poll a cancellable graph query job: running (+chunk progress),
succeeded (+graph result), or canceled. Failed jobs raise HTTP 400.

post.description:
Cancel an in-flight graph query job: stops API-side processing/download
and best-effort cancels the underlying backend statement(s).

Transpile an OpenCypher query to SQL without executing it.

Returns only the transpiled SQL for review before execution. Warehouse-only:
a backend that speaks Cypher natively has no SQL to show.

Discover the node types and relationship types a datasource exposes.

Used when creating a GraphContext to populate the available types. A SQL
warehouse runs ``SELECT DISTINCT`` over the two tables; a native graph
database reads its own label catalog.
Generate a random graph (dev mode only).

delete.description:
Clear all data (dev mode only, superuser only).

Alias of ``POST /api/admin/environment/clear`` kept for the dev generator
page. Same double gate: dev mode *and* superuser (the dev default identity
is a superuser in the shipped ``.env.example``), and the audit trail is
preserved so the ``admin.clear_all`` entry outlives the wipe.

get.description:
What this context can do with precomputed graphs.

Deliberately not a listing: it answers "can anything here be written, and by
which providers", so the frontend knows whether to show its write panel. It
never enumerates entries.

Resolve a precomputed graph. Requires read access to the context.

Returns the payload under `Content-Encoding: gzip`. When the resolving
provider held encoded bytes already, they are passed through untouched:
Starlette's GZipMiddleware forwards a body that already declares an
encoding, so nothing decompresses or re-serializes the graph server-side.

put.description: Publish a graph the client already holds. Superuser only, where supported.

delete.description:
Delete a precomputed graph. Superuser only, where the provider supports it.

A precomputed graph is shared, so removing one affects every viewer, and
(unlike a style preset) authoring one is not tied to context ownership in
the first place.

get.description: List this context's presets. Requires read access to the context.
Read one preset. Requires read access to the context.

put.description:
Create or update a preset. Requires write access to the context.

Overwriting keeps the original author: a preset is a named slot, and whoever
created it stays the one who can delete it.

delete.description:
Delete a preset. Only its creator — or a superuser — may do so.

Ownership lives inside the stored file, so this reads the preset before
deleting it. That is one extra round trip, and the reason the listing does
not report owners: doing it there would cost one request per preset.

List all databases in a catalog.

Get the schema of a table.
Preview table data.

This is useful when tables are created after the service starts,

patch.description:
Edit the case: title, description, tags, case type and fields (merged; null removes one),
stage, assignee, dates, SLA hours, settings and view state. `status` moves between open
and analysis; only a decision closes a case. An agent's status change arrives as a
suggested `status_change`. 409 `CASE_CLOSED` on a closed case.

delete.description: **People only**: an agent token gets 403 `AGENT_FORBIDDEN` (deleting a case (05 §6)).

post.description:
Human only (06 §1): appends a decision with its own hash. An outcome that
closes the case freezes it (every mutation answers 409 until reopened); with
four eyes it waits for another person's review first.

**People only**: an agent token gets 403 `AGENT_FORBIDDEN` (a decision is a person's (05 §6, 06 §1)).

Four eyes: approve or reject a pending decision (never one's own).

**People only**: an agent token gets 403 `AGENT_FORBIDDEN` (four eyes are a second person's (06 §1)).

closed → analysis, human only; journaled as ``case.reopened``.

**People only**: an agent token gets 403 `AGENT_FORBIDDEN` (reopening a decided case (05 §3)).

Package (json) or csv; verifies every decision's hash and is audited with

Add an item. JSON body (`ItemCreate`) for text or JSON content, links, saved queries and

A new ``table/result`` item: the tables joined by the key column; its
provenance names the parents.

Diff by key of two tables, or of two runs of one query: rows only on one
side, rows whose shared columns changed, and how many are the same.

enrichment in one go: each gets ``mapping.as`` with a spec over its columns.

Remove an item from the case (people only). It is
marked deleted, so the journal and the versions it pinned keep their history; its blobs go
when the case is deleted.

**People only**: an agent token gets 403 `AGENT_FORBIDDEN` (deleting material (agents add and version, never remove)).

**People only**: an agent token gets 403 `AGENT_FORBIDDEN` (a person restores a removed item, as only people remove them (UX-1)).

Every version of an item, oldest first: number, sha256, size, content type, author, run
metadata for queries and pin.

**People only**: an agent token gets 403 `AGENT_FORBIDDEN` (a person rejects suggestions (05 §6)).

Annotations of the case (role, tag, group, same_as, hypothesis, hypothesis_status,
status_change, task, decision_proposal) with status, author and reason. Filter with
`kind`, `status` and `target` (an entity or item id).

post.description:
Annotate entities or items. A person's annotation is confirmed; an agent's arrives suggested
for the kinds the case lists (and always for a decision_proposal). A confirmed role
replaces the entity's previous one unless the case type allows several. Tasks and their
edits also work on a closed case.

patch.description:
Edit an annotation's value, targets or reason. An agent edits only the tasks it wrote or
that are assigned to it (403 `TASK_NOT_YOURS`).

delete.description:
Remove an annotation (people only).

**People only**: an agent token gets 403 `AGENT_FORBIDDEN` (deleting annotations (agents add, never remove)).

post.description: **People only**: an agent token gets 403 `AGENT_FORBIDDEN` (a person confirms suggestions (05 §6)).
**People only**: an agent token gets 403 `AGENT_FORBIDDEN` (a person rejects suggestions (05 §6)).

A rejected suggestion is a suggestion again (people only): 409 `NOT_REJECTED` otherwise.
Nothing was applied when it was rejected, so nothing is undone.

**People only**: an agent token gets 403 `AGENT_FORBIDDEN` (a person takes back a rejection (UX-1)).

Confirm or reject several suggestions at once (people only). All are checked first; one
unknown id or forbidden kind fails the call. Ones no longer suggested come back in `skipped`.

**People only**: an agent token gets 403 `AGENT_FORBIDDEN` (a person confirms or rejects suggestions in bulk (UX-1)).

get.description:
The unified case graph (identity keys and confirmed same_as applied), or
one item's with ``item_id``.

What one graph item puts on the canvas (snapshot, identity keys, edge
semantics); the browser unifies these with ``unifyGraph.ts``.

post.description:
Follow the money on the case's unified graph: from `seed_edge_ids` or a `seed_node`, forward
or backward, with an allocation rule, layers, dwell time, minimum amount, time window
and stop types (unset values come from the case type's trace defaults). Returns the
exits, the coverage and the method stamp; journaled as `trace.run`.

Paths between two entities of the unified graph: shortest, weighted, k-shortest or earliest
arrival. Journaled as `path.run`.

Entity resolution on the unified graph: entities sharing a blocking
attribute with similar names become ``same_as`` annotations, suggested (a
person confirms them in the inspector).

Journal what the browser ran on its own graph: `trace.run`, `path.run`, `nodes.promoted`
(enrichment nodes added to the canvas) or `metric.saved` (a metric saved as a property).
Other kinds answer 422 `EVENT_KIND_NOT_ALLOWED`.

Items whose title, description, tags, query or latest text contain `q` (case-insensitive

actions, its fields, deadlines and what the agent reads first. Data, not code.

CypherQueryRequest.description:
Request to execute an OpenCypher query.

Note: The query should include its own LIMIT clause if needed.
The backend respects whatever LIMIT is specified in the Cypher query.

CypherQueryResponse.title: CypherQueryResponse
CypherQueryResponse.description: Response from an OpenCypher query execution.

CypherTranspileRequest.title: CypherTranspileRequest
CypherTranspileRequest.description: Request to transpile an OpenCypher query (without execution).

DatasetsResponse.title: DatasetsResponse
DatasetsResponse.description:
Tables the warehouse offers for building a graph context.

`tables` is every table in the configured catalog/schema pairs. Which of
them is the edge table and which is the node table is the user's call, made
in the picker — the two lists below only carry the name-based guess
(`*edge*` / `*node*`) so existing callers keep working; nothing should
*restrict* a choice to them.

DecisionTask.title: DecisionTask
DecisionTask.description:
A follow-up the decision sets in motion: one of the type's ``actions``
(its label is the title) or a free one with a ``title``.

EdgeStructure.title: EdgeStructure
EdgeStructure.description: Structural column mapping for edge table.

EnrichmentEdgeKey.title: EnrichmentEdgeKey
EnrichmentEdgeKey.description:
How an enrichment file's rows find edges: by the edge id (``key_column``)
or by its two endpoints (node ids, normalized like the key) and, optionally,
its relationship type. Endpoint rows match either direction.

EntityCase.title: EntityCase
EntityCase.description: A case where an entity is present or of interest (06 P7).

EntityResolutionRequest.title: EntityResolutionRequest
EntityResolutionRequest.description:
Blocking attributes and name properties of ``/analysis/er``; the
defaults of ``services/entity_resolution.py`` when omitted.

ExtraColumnDefinition.title: ExtraColumnDefinition
ExtraColumnDefinition.description: Definition for an extra column to generate.

FileEnrichmentSpec.title: FileEnrichmentSpec
FileEnrichmentSpec.description:
How a file's rows add properties to the nodes (or edges) of a graph: in a
case, a ``table`` item with ``mapping.as = enrichment``; in an exploration, an
entry of its overlay. Rows are keyed by ``key_column`` (normalized with
``normalize``, then cut to the first ``key_digits`` digits when set); a node of
``match_node_types`` (empty or ``*`` = every type) matches by its id or a
property. A value already on the node wins unless ``overwrite``; the losing
value is recorded as a conflict. Edges match by ``edge_key``.

default_behaviors.title: Default Behaviors
default_behaviors.description: Default graph behavior settings applied when this context is opened (e.g. {'viewMode': '3d'}). Passed through opaquely; the frontend validates keys against its own schema. A saved exploration overrides these.

cluster_programs.title: Cluster Programs
cluster_programs.description: Context-level cluster programs shared by all explorations of this context. Passed through opaquely; the frontend owns the shape.

context_menu_actions.title: Context Menu Actions
context_menu_actions.description: Context-level configurable context-menu actions (open-url, copy-text, run-query-template). Passed through opaquely; the frontend owns the shape.

metric_definitions.title: Metric Definitions
metric_definitions.description: Writer-authored custom metrics (per-node/edge JavaScript evaluated in the frontend's sandboxed worker). Only returned to users with write access.

GraphJobProgress.title: GraphJobProgress
GraphJobProgress.description: Chunk-download progress for an in-flight graph query job.

partial.description: A renderable intermediate result — edges plus nodes carrying only their structural columns — published while the job is still fetching properties. Lets the client draw the graph before the job completes.

partial_seq.title: Partial Seq
partial_seq.description: Increments on each published partial. The client polls far more often than partials are produced, so it applies a partial only when this advances.

GraphJobStatusResponse.title: GraphJobStatusResponse
GraphJobStatusResponse.description:
Poll response for an in-flight graph query job.

``running`` carries chunk-download ``progress``; ``succeeded`` carries the
``result`` graph (and ``transpiled_sql`` for cypher). A failed job surfaces
as HTTP 400; a cancelled one as ``status="canceled"``.

GraphJobSubmitResponse.title: GraphJobSubmitResponse
GraphJobSubmitResponse.description: Response to submitting a cancellable graph/cypher query job.

GraphOverlay.title: GraphOverlay
GraphOverlay.description:
The user's layer of an exploration (BYOD-2): nodes, edges and enrichment files on top
of the context's answer. Saved beside the snapshot, never inside it.

GraphQueryRequest.title: GraphQueryRequest
GraphQueryRequest.description:
Request to execute a graph query (SQL).

Note: The query should include its own LIMIT clause if needed.
The backend respects whatever LIMIT is specified in the query.

properties_deferred.title: Properties Deferred
properties_deferred.description: True when nodes were returned without their properties (nodes_mode='types'). Tells the client to schedule background enrichment via /nodes/batch; false keeps the historical contract.

GraphSnapshot.title: GraphSnapshot
GraphSnapshot.description: Full graph state snapshot (nodes + edges with positions and properties).

examples.description: Opened by the disputes queue; the same external_ref again returns this case.
examples.title: Chargeback CB-4471-0912

InvestigationDecisionCreate.title: InvestigationDecisionCreate
InvestigationDecisionCreate.description:
06 §1: one of the case type's outcomes (or a free one when the type has
none), on the whole case or on some entities, with its rationale, the pinned
evidence it rests on and the follow-up tasks it sets in motion.

examples.rationale: Bust-out pattern: volume x8 in two weeks, then chargebacks (E1, E2).

InvestigationPage.title: InvestigationPage
InvestigationPage.description:
A page of the queue: ``total`` matches the filters, ``counts`` are over
every case the caller reads (the counter cards).

ItemState.title: ItemState
ItemState.description: How an item is shown (view only, never a version).

MetricDefinition.title: MetricDefinition
MetricDefinition.description:
A writer-authored JavaScript metric evaluated per node/edge.

The code runs only in the frontend, inside a sandboxed Web Worker with a
hard timeout. The server never executes it — it stores the definition and
validates its shape. Definitions are returned only to users with write
access on the context (see routers.graph_contexts.context_to_response), so
read-only users never receive, let alone run, another user's code.

node_ids.title: Node Ids
node_ids.description: Node ids to fetch. Capped so one batch stays a bounded query; the client chunks larger sets.

columns.title: Columns
columns.description: Optional subset of property columns to fetch. Every name is validated against the context's configured node_properties, so this can only ever NARROW the projection — never widen it or reach columns the context does not expose. Unknown names are ignored. Omit to fetch everything the context exposes; that is expensive on wide tables (a 100-column table costs ~36 MB for 19k nodes), which is what this field exists to avoid.

NodeBatchRequest.title: NodeBatchRequest
NodeBatchRequest.description: Fetch properties for a known set of node ids (progressive load).

NodeStructure.title: NodeStructure
NodeStructure.description: Structural column mapping for node table.

OverlayEnrichment.title: OverlayEnrichment
OverlayEnrichment.description: An enrichment file in an exploration's layer: its spec and parsed rows (first per key).

OverlayImport.title: OverlayImport
OverlayImport.description: Nodes and edges that came in together (a mapped file, pasted JSON), removable as one.

PermissionInspection.title: PermissionInspection
PermissionInspection.description:
Why a user can or cannot do each catalog action — the admin
inspector's payload, produced by services.permissions.inspect_user.

properties_deferred.title: Properties Deferred
properties_deferred.description: Always false for a precomputed graph — writes are refused while node properties are still being enriched, so an entry is never half-filled.

PrecomputedGraphData.title: PrecomputedGraphData
PrecomputedGraphData.description:
The graph a precomputed entry replays.

Deliberately the *API* node/edge shape rather than the snapshot shape, so a
precomputed graph feeds the frontend store without a field-by-field remap.
It is GraphResponse minus `metadata`, which is query timing and meaningless
once replayed.

No node positions: a precomputed graph is data, and layout runs fresh on
load. Positions with their surrounding visual state are what explorations
and their snapshots are for.

PrecomputedGraphEntry.title: PrecomputedGraphEntry
PrecomputedGraphEntry.description:
What a write reports back about the entry it just stored.

There is no listing endpoint to return these in bulk — entries are addressed
by name, and enumerating them is the one operation that does not survive
scale. Richer metadata lives inside the payload itself.

PrecomputedGraphSource.title: PrecomputedGraphSource
PrecomputedGraphSource.description:
Where a precomputed graph came from.

Both fields are optional, and a `source` omitted entirely is valid: a graph
assembled by a batch job from Delta tables, or built by hand, never had a
query to record. `kind="manual"` is how such an entry says so, which is not
the same as a query-derived entry whose query was lost.

`datasource_type`/`datasource_name` used to live here and were removed: an
entry is already scoped to a context, the context knows its own datasource,
and nothing ever read the copies back. Worse, repointing a context at another
datasource would have left them silently lying.

ProceduralBFSOptions.title: ProceduralBFSOptions
ProceduralBFSOptions.description:
Fine-grained toggles for gsql2rsql's procedural BFS renderer.

Field names and defaults mirror ``gsql2rsql.ProceduralBFSOptimizations``.
Flags only take effect when ``vlp_rendering_mode == "procedural"``. Note
``undirected_doubled_adjacency`` and ``undirected_union_all`` are mutually
exclusive — enabling both raises ``ValueError`` in the transpiler.

PropertyColumn.title: PropertyColumn
PropertyColumn.description: Definition of a property column (non-structural metadata).

QueryMetadata.title: QueryMetadata
QueryMetadata.description: Timing metadata for query execution stages (all values in milliseconds).

RandomGraphRequest.title: RandomGraphRequest
RandomGraphRequest.description: Request to generate a random graph using NetworkX.

ReportCreate.title: ReportCreate
ReportCreate.description: ``POST …/reports``: render an org library template into a markdown document.

ResolverStatus.title: ResolverStatus
ResolverStatus.description: Provenance of Databricks group membership lookups (admin banner).

SchemaDiscoveryRequest.title: SchemaDiscoveryRequest
SchemaDiscoveryRequest.description:
Request to discover the types a datasource exposes.

A SQL warehouse needs the two tables and their structural columns to run
``SELECT DISTINCT``; a native graph database reads its own label catalog and
ignores all three, which is why they are optional.

SchemaDiscoveryResponse.title: SchemaDiscoveryResponse
SchemaDiscoveryResponse.description: Response with distinct node and relationship types from tables.

SchemaDriftFinding.title: SchemaDriftFinding
SchemaDriftFinding.description: One detected difference between a context's stored snapshot and the live table.

SchemaDriftProposal.title: SchemaDriftProposal
SchemaDriftProposal.description:
The resync payload — echo this back through PUT to apply it.

``node_types``/``relationship_types`` are ``None`` unless the check was run
with ``check_types=true``; ``None`` already means "leave unchanged" on
``GraphContextUpdate``, so this can be forwarded verbatim.

SchemaDriftResponse.title: SchemaDriftResponse
SchemaDriftResponse.description:
Full drift report for a context. A read-only diff — never an HTTP failure
on its own; an unreachable table surfaces as a `TABLE_NOT_FOUND` finding.

SchemaDriftTable.title: SchemaDriftTable
SchemaDriftTable.description:
Live state of one side's table, as seen by the drift check.

``table_name`` is ``None`` on the node side of a nodeless (triple-store-only)
context — the virtual node table is derived from edges and cannot drift.

StylePreset.title: StylePreset
StylePreset.description: What gets written to the volume, and what a read returns.

StylePresetEntry.title: StylePresetEntry
StylePresetEntry.description:
One row of the preset listing.

Only what a directory listing reports — no `created_by`, because ownership
lives inside each file and reading every one of them to build a list would
be a request per preset. Delete checks ownership server-side instead.

StylePresetSettings.title: StylePresetSettings
StylePresetSettings.description:
The presentation subset of an exploration's state.

Every field here already exists in `ExplorationState` and is produced and
consumed by the same frontend code, so a preset and an exploration can never
describe the same thing two different ways.

Deliberately excluded: nodes, edges, filters, viewport, the query and its
transpile options, clusters, communities and similarity — a preset never
carries which data is loaded, otherwise applying one would silently hide
nodes and the graph would look like it came back incomplete. Also excluded:
context-menu actions, which persist per-context on
graph_contexts.context_menu_actions, never per-preset.

The server does not interpret any of it. Shapes are owned by the frontend
(`buildStylePreset`/`applyStylePreset` in stores/graph.ts) and validated
there; typing them here would mean two definitions drifting apart.

nodes_mode.title: Nodes Mode
nodes_mode.description: 'full' returns nodes with all configured properties (default, unchanged behaviour). 'types' returns only node_id and node_type — everything needed to render — leaving properties null so the client can paint the graph immediately and fetch properties in the background via /nodes/batch.

TableChartSpec.title: TableChartSpec
TableChartSpec.description: A table seen as a chart (06 §2b AQ2): ``x`` and ``series`` name its columns.

TableCompareRequest.title: TableCompareRequest
TableCompareRequest.description: Two tables, or two runs of one query (same ``item_id``, two ``version``s).

TableJoinRequest.title: TableJoinRequest
TableJoinRequest.description: Join two or more table items by ``key_column`` (the first shared column when omitted).

TablePromoteRequest.title: TablePromoteRequest
TablePromoteRequest.description:
``as = enrichment`` (key_column, match_node_types, match_source, key_digits) or
``as = graph`` (source_column, target_column, source_type, target_type, edge_type,
normalize, amount_prop, time_prop); options missing fall back to the first columns.

TableQueryRequest.title: TableQueryRequest
TableQueryRequest.description:
Request to run a generic query and return raw tabular rows.

Unlike CypherQueryRequest, the query is NOT required to return edges
(RETURN r). Any projection is allowed; the result is returned as
columns + rows for display in a table.

TableQueryResponse.title: TableQueryResponse
TableQueryResponse.description:
Response from a generic tabular query.

``status`` distinguishes the two outcomes of the cancellable submit flow:
- ``"succeeded"``: query finished within the submit wait window; ``columns``
  and ``rows`` hold the result (the historical fast-path shape).
- ``"running"``: query is still executing; ``columns``/``rows`` are empty and
  ``statement_id`` identifies it for polling (``GET .../query/table/{id}``)
  and cancellation (``POST .../query/table/{id}/cancel``).

TableQueryStatusResponse.title: TableQueryStatusResponse
TableQueryStatusResponse.description:
Poll response for an in-flight table query.

Mirrors :class:`TableQueryResponse` but for the ``GET`` status endpoint:
``status="running"`` while executing, ``status="succeeded"`` with data once
complete. A FAILED/timed-out statement surfaces as an HTTP 400 instead; a
CANCELED one as ``status="canceled"``.

TemplateOptions.title: TemplateOptions
TemplateOptions.description: Execution options embedded in a query template.

TemplateParameter.title: TemplateParameter
TemplateParameter.description: A parameter for a query template.

TraceRequest.title: TraceRequest
TraceRequest.description:
Seed = ``seed_edge_ids`` or the outgoing (forward) / incoming (backward)
edges of ``seed_node``. Defaults are the T5 ones (README Q4).

agentToken.description: A personal agent token (`glt_…`, Agents page of the account menu). It acts with the access of the person who created it; a case-scoped token reaches only its cases.

forwardedEmail.name: X-Forwarded-Email
forwardedEmail.description: Set by the authenticating proxy (Databricks Apps, an SSO gateway). Clients never send it themselves outside dev mode.
